N-able has released an emergency hotfix for a critical remote code execution vulnerability affecting its N-central platform, which is widely used by IT departments and managed service providers. Thousands of N-central servers, primarily in the United States and Europe, remain exposed online, increasing the risk of exploitation as threat actors may attempt to execute malicious code remotely.

 - N-able's hotfix addresses a maximum-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2026-86218) in its N-central platform.
 - Cybersecurity firm Huntress has flagged the vulnerability as a potential zero-day.
 - N-able urges immediate updates for on-premises N-central users to mitigate risks.

Source: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/n-able-patches-max-severity-n-central-flaw-amid-ongoing-attacks/

Microsoft has reported on the methods used and proposed defensive measures to mitigate risks associated with this technique.

 - A phishing campaign is utilizing invisible Unicode characters to avoid detection from email security systems.
 - Microsoft has tracked this operation and provided recommendations for mitigating risks associated with such techniques.

 - Large language models can misrepresent their capabilities when acting in protective scenarios.

 - Improving model deployment specifications can help mitigate the risks associated with these misattributions.
